question: What is Footnote?
answer: Footnote is a help chatbot for your website. It answers your customers from your own FAQs and help articles, names where each answer came from, asks when it isn't sure, and hands off to a person when it can't help.

question: Does Footnote use AI or an LLM?
answer: No. Footnote uses PostgreSQL full-text search: no LLM, no embeddings and no AI APIs. That means no per-message AI cost, and it never writes an answer that isn't in your content.

question: How much does Footnote cost to run?
answer: There is no AI bill. Answers come from full-text search in your database, so there is no per-message API cost and no LLM usage to pay for.

question: Where do the chatbot's answers come from?
answer: Only from your own FAQs and documents. Every answer quotes one of them and names the source, so visitors can see where it came from. The chatbot never answers from anything else.

question: What happens when the chatbot isn't sure?
answer: When the match is weak, it asks instead of guessing. It shows the best answer with "Did you mean" suggestions so the visitor can pick the right question.

question: What happens when the chatbot can't answer?
answer: It says honestly that it couldn't find an answer, offers related questions, and shows your handoff options so the visitor can reach a person. The question also appears in Analytics so you can add an answer.

question: Does it understand different ways of asking?
answer: Yes. Synonyms link the words visitors use to the words in your content, like "money back" to "refund". It also handles small talk, small typos and follow-ups like "what about international orders?" in context.

question: How do I set up a chatbot?
answer: Sign up and your dashboard opens. Create a chatbot, add your FAQs and documents, test it like a visitor, choose how visitors reach a person, then paste one line of code on your website. The setup guide in the dashboard ticks the steps off as you go.

question: How long does it take to go live?
answer: Three steps: add your content, test it in the preview, and paste one script tag on your site. The widget does the rest.

question: How do I add content to the chatbot?
answer: Write FAQs in your customers' own words, upload files, import a web page by its address, or paste text. The chatbot only answers from what you add.

question: What file types can I upload?
answer: PDF, Word (DOCX), Markdown, plain text, and CSV, up to 20 MB per file. A CSV with question and answer columns imports as FAQs. Scanned PDFs without a text layer can't be read, because there is no OCR.

question: Can I import my existing help pages?
answer: Yes. Paste a web page address and its text is imported once as a document. Pages that need JavaScript to show their content come out empty, so paste their text instead.

question: How do I test the chatbot before going live?
answer: Use Test in the dashboard. Ask real questions, including vague and misspelled ones. Each answer shows its source and match score. If the wrong answer wins, reword the FAQ question or add keywords. Test questions are not counted in analytics.

question: How do I add the chatbot to my website?
answer: Paste one line of code before </body> on every page that should show the chat button. The Install tab in your dashboard has the exact line with your chatbot's id.

question: Can other websites show my chatbot?
answer: Only if you allow it. List your website addresses in the Install tab and browsers refuse to show your chatbot on any other site.

question: Can I change how the chat looks?
answer: Yes. In Customize you can set the theme, colors, button position and icon, the header title, the greeting and up to four starter questions, with a live preview.

question: Can visitors talk to a real person?
answer: Yes. When the chatbot can't help, or a visitor asks for a person, it offers the channels you switch on: a live chat with your team, a reply by email, WhatsApp, or your contact form.

question: How does live chat with an agent work?
answer: The visitor picks Chat with an agent and the chat window starts talking to your team instead of the bot. You answer from the Handoff tab in your dashboard, and your replies appear in their chat window within a few seconds.

question: How does Get a reply by email work?
answer: The visitor leaves their question and email address in the chat. It lands in your Handoff inbox and your team gets an email alert. Your reply from the dashboard is emailed to the visitor, and their email replies come back into the same conversation.

question: How will my team know a visitor is waiting?
answer: New messages show in the dashboard's notification bell with a pop-up, and each new conversation is emailed to the address you set under Handoff.

question: What does Analytics show?
answer: For the last 7, 30 or 90 days: conversations, questions, how many were answered, the questions it couldn't answer grouped by wording, the most searched topics and the most used articles. Turn any unanswered question into an FAQ in one click.

question: Can I run more than one chatbot?
answer: Yes. One account can run several chatbots, each with its own content, settings and link, for example one per website.

question: Can my teammates use the same dashboard?
answer: Yes. Your organization is your workspace, so teammates who join it see and manage the same chatbots.

question: Is visitor data kept private?
answer: Email addresses and phone numbers in questions are replaced with [email] and [phone] before questions are stored for analytics. A visitor's chat in progress is kept in their own browser until they close the tab.
